around.headline: Six arrested with MDMA worth Rs 5.48 crore in Bengaluru
around.summary: Police seized MDMA valued at Rs 5.48 crore and arrested six people, per ThePrint and NDTV. Never carry or hold a package for someone you don't know well; report suspected dealing to 112.

around.headline: Fake medicine racket: SIT arrests another accused
around.summary: The SIT probing the counterfeit-medicine racket has made another arrest, per The Times of India. Buy medicines from a chemist you trust and check the batch number and packaging.

around.headline: Auto driver held after fare row turns physical with two women
around.summary: A cancelled-booking and fare dispute ended in a fight on a Bengaluru road; the driver was held for assaulting the women, per Deccan Herald and The Times of India. Note the vehicle number and complain rather than fight it out on the road.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: BMRDA notifies new mobility road grid for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region
around.summary: The road grid aims to prevent congestion as the city expands, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. Worth checking if you plan to buy or rent on the city's outskirts.

around.headline: BMTC buses to get 'smart eyes' for safety and passenger tracking
around.summary: BMTC buses will get smart cameras for safer travel and passenger tracking, per The Times of India. Regular bus commuters may see better safety monitoring onboard.

around.headline: After High Court nudge, civic body to crack down on non-compliant PGs
around.summary: Occupants of non-compliant PGs are to get three weeks, per Live Law. If you live in a PG, ask your owner about compliance now.

around.summary: Delhi is bringing stringent curbs as pollution season nears, per Hindustan Times. If you drive to Delhi, make sure your pollution certificate is valid.

street_smart.title: Someone you recently met online offers you ₹5,000 to receive a sealed courier at your address and hand it to a 'friend' who will collect it in the evening. He says it's just 'personal items' and there's nothing to worry about. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: ThePrint / NDTV: 'Six arrested with MDMA worth Rs 5.48 crore in Bengaluru' (2026-09-30).
street_smart.situation: Money is tight and the task seems easy. The parcel is due today, and he says he'll send the collector's number later.

choices.text: Accept — you're only receiving and handing over a sealed box.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Drug networks and fraudsters use unwitting locals as couriers so the parcel is traced to your address, not theirs. Under the NDPS Act, possession or handling of contraband can lead to arrest even if you never opened the box.

choices.text: Accept, but open the box first and repack it before the handover.
choices.feedback: Opening it doesn't protect you: if it contains contraband, you've now handled it and your fingerprints are on it. Handling a suspicious parcel at all is the problem.

choices.text: Decline, don't accept the parcel, block the contact, and report the offer to the cyber helpline 1930 or 112 with screenshots.
choices.feedback: Refusing keeps your address out of the chain, and the chat screenshots give police something to act on. Easy money for a no-questions errand is the classic recruitment pitch for courier and mule schemes.

choices.text: Take the parcel but ask for the ₹5,000 in advance as insurance.
choices.feedback: The advance doesn't protect you legally; it only shows you were paid to handle it, which can look like knowing involvement.

takeaways: Never receive, hold or forward a parcel for someone you don't know well, whatever the fee.
Report suspicious offers to 112 or the cyber helpline 1930, and keep screenshots.
If a parcel you didn't order arrives, don't open it, refuse delivery, and inform the police.

quiz.question: How much MDMA was reportedly seized in the Bengaluru bust in which six people were arrested?
quiz.why: MDMA is a synthetic drug regulated under the NDPS Act, 1985, which treats quantity thresholds as key to how severe the punishment is.

quiz.question: Which body has notified the new mobility road grid for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region?
quiz.why: BMRDA, the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority, plans development beyond the city's core limits.

quiz.question: From October 1, which vehicles will be refused fuel in Delhi under the curbs mentioned in the news?
quiz.why: PUCC stands for Pollution Under Control Certificate, issued after an emissions test.

quiz.question: Which is the largest state in India by area?
quiz.why: Rajasthan covers about 3.42 lakh sq km, roughly 10% of India's area.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
quiz.why: Oxygen is about 21%; argon is the third most abundant at roughly 0.9%.
